_readme: Andhra Pradesh, indicator by indicator, since bifurcation. Every figure is transcribed verbatim from a government publication and carries the document, the table and the agency that originated it. Nothing is modelled, indexed or adjusted. The only arithmetic we do is subtraction between two printed years, and where we do it we name both years so anyone can redo it.
_bifurcation_note: Andhra Pradesh was divided on 2 June 2014. Some tables print the undivided state for earlier years and the residuary state afterwards; those years are marked and are never compared with later ones. Where the national statistics office has itself back-cast the residuary state, we say so on that indicator.
_tenure_note: Financial years end on 31 March, but governments changed in May and June. We label each year by the government that held office for most of it: 2014-15 to 2018-19 the TDP government, 2019-20 to 2023-24 the YSRCP government, 2024-25 onward the TDP-led NDA government. Each of those first years is really ten months of that government.
_arithmetic_note: Where we show a change under a government, it is the difference between two figures the source printed, and both years are named. We never compare across the 2014 bifurcation, and we never fill a missing year.

_stage_note: Not every figure is a final one. Where the source prints a marker we carry it: A means audited accounts, RE a revised estimate, BE a budget estimate, PE a provisional estimate. Estimates are drawn lighter than accounts everywhere on this page and are never compared with an audited figure without saying so. The Reserve Bank's most recent audited fiscal year is 2022-23; its 2023-24 and 2024-25 fiscal figures are the state's own estimates, which is why they can differ from the audited numbers on our finances page. Both are official; they are answering different questions.
_dropped_note: Two series had a final column that covered only part of a year — market borrowings to September, national highway length to December. A part-year figure drawn beside full years reads as a collapse that did not happen, and a footnote inside a bar chart is invisible. We removed those points rather than draw them, and say so here.

_source_caution: One caution about the fiscal figures on this page. They come from the Reserve Bank's Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, which reprints figures the states themselves produce. Where we have been able to check a year against the audited Finance Accounts, the Handbook has matched them closely — except for 2017-18 and 2018-19 own tax revenue, where it runs 5.9% and 1.1% above the audited figure and prints no marker to say the number is anything other than final. We do not know what basis those two readings use. Where a figure matters we show the state's own audited accounts alongside, and we say when the two disagree rather than choosing one quietly.
